matches.title: Swarmer fallen solo | No Accelerator, Ranger, Turret, or Minigunner
matches.snippet: That's right, Executioner is all you need for hidden detection, and while the triumph screen does hide the one in the top left corner, I only needed three maxed Executioners, and I guess a max Medic too, but it contributed basically nothing for damage. Executioner was my early game after tanking first 4 waves, although I'm pretty confident you can place it sooner and be fine in terms of farming for level 4 by wave 13. Why the Executioner is so efficient is because of the new targeting settings, specifically farthest, although last can also work pretty well on long straight paths if you have towers to cover leaked enemies (including hiddens), and even random can work somewhat well. This works because the Executioner hitting something with an axe only counts as a bounce once it has hit it's intended target at least once, then everything past that will be a bounce, or extra hit on either the target or other enemy, then return to the tower after using up all bounces. The hitbox of the axe is always active from the moment it is thrown though, so by setting the targeting to farthest or last and making sure the tower is placed a bit close to a straight path, you can set it up so it goes for a target pretty far from it where the axe will hit many other enemies while doing so without needing to return. matches.title: What's the meta Loadout in TDS?
matches.snippet: Its hard to make a meta Loadout considering all modes(e.g. Normal, Hardcore, events, Pizza Party, etc.), but this is the meta Loadout I use(and yes I grinded for engineer no joke, I learned my lesson about shitposting for the pain to grind for Engineer): Engineer. This is the DPS game choice, the backbone of this meta Loadout. Does 2700(450 DPS * 6 Placement limit) DPS in total and that can kill Fallen King in around a minute if you do the math. Although it's Sentries can't deal with hiddens and can't get buffed by DJ and Commander, the gas prices get cheaper and Engineers damage is good enough to kill a shadow boss. It was my idiot ness earlier for saying engineer can't kill a shadow boss. If used properly shadow boss isn't a big deal. Farm. This is the eco choice. Always use farm over cowboy for income generation. I mean yeah Golden Cowboy has shown to make more money than farm, but it depends on the enemies coming. In badlands, it is rich, but in Molten mode, it's poor. At least with farm you don't have to worry about the enemy health for cash. DJ. This is the choice for support. The problem with Commander is Engineer's Sentries, our main DPS, can't be buffed by him. However the gas prices can be cheaper with DJ. matches.title: Guide to understanding strategies
matches.snippet: ( !! FOR NEW PLAYERS !! ) Ah, you just got logged on to discord, found out that TDS had a server so you join it, but wait! You found Party-que! but you don't understand what these players are using what does LF Mega Fallen or Duo Fallen Strat means. That's where I come in! Strategies Ah, the most used way of winning Hardcore, Events and other stuff. But little Billy here doesn't know what these terms mean. refer to the guide below to understand. matches.title: Rambling about a tower - the DJ Booth
matches.snippet: Sooooo… the DJ Booth. A clear A-Tier tower, powerful but not to the point of being a hard carry. The DJ Booth is useful in essentially every single gamemode and event, save for Rotfield. In Normal, DJ sees the least use, as you generally don’t need expensive towers to beat it easily. In Molten, DJ is always a good option, and is in a very good balance here of ‘great, but not using it doesn’t feel too much like a hindrance’, depending on the strategy you use. In Fallen, DJ shines more than in the prior modes. This time, you’re aiming for more costly towers like the Accelerator if you want to beat Fallen King reliably, and the DJ Booth excels in getting these high DPS towers. The range buff shouldn’t be underestimated either; in fact, it’s extremely strong and may even rival the discount buff. In Hardcore, it’s almost required to bring along a DJ Booth, though my lack of experience outside of strategies that always use DJ means that I don’t really know how hard DJless Hardcore is. Same goes for Polluted Wasteland and PWII. DJ is essentially the same in all events: extremely beneficial, almost to Hardcore’s extent for some. Nights 1 and 2 are an exception, where you wouldn’t use DJ in the former and commonly only go for Level 3 in the latter. DJ Booth has interesting upgrades. matches.title: Top 10 tips to become a TDS pro
matches.snippet: 👋 Hey, newer players! Here are some tips for becoming a TDS pro. These tips include the best strategies for making tons of coins. Tip #1: Always use Cowboy for early game, especially in quad. Quad modes have Health Scaling, which means tougher enemies. Cowboy gives you the money you need to deal with such enemies. Tip #2: If you have few towers unlocked, make sure to always have 5 towers on a loadout. Get towers like Demoman to have all 5 slots used. It looks better to pros when you have all 5 slots used than to only use 2 or three, even if they are better towers. matches.title: How versatile and useful is Hacker really?
matches.snippet: Hacker has 4 different abilities: boosting enemy rewards, cloning, hacking enemies, and slowness but how useful is the tower compared to other towers that could use its slot, like DPS towers? The top and bottom paths costs totals of $96K and $80K respectively. It's been only a day since it came out but so far I don't think its worthwhile in most situations. It's slowness is 15 to 25% which isn't a lot, stunning and freezing towers can do better. It's eco boost definitely doesn't compensate for its very high cost. Unit DPS is inherently low and inconsistent, since it takes a long time for high health enemies has to die first before becoming one with a fraction of its original health. Cloning is imo, the one noteworthy ability, but costs 65% or 90% of the tower cost for the top and bottom paths respectively and can only be used once every 60 secs. So the only tower really worth cloning is Gatling Gun. Thus one really useful for the final waves of the special gamemodes or hardcore. So far I would definitely not recommend bringing it to Fallen and only bring it to special gamemodes or hardcore, to boost much needed single target DPS but only if you or someone else brings Gatling Gun. How versatile and useful is Hacker really?

matches.title: Not the TDS I know | Why consumables are a bad mechanic
matches.snippet: I am going to talk about why consumables are the worst mechanic to ever have been added to the game. I will explain what this does to the general gameplay and how it may affect the future of the game if it not heavily changed or removed. I will offer solutions to every issue I point out afterwards, as I do believe this mechanic can add something meaningful to the game, but the devs messed it up in every single manner and it was overall unnecessary, and I believe many other things should of been prioritized over this. How will consumables affect gameplay in matches? Firsly, the fact that these are just a direct upgrade to a player's arsenal is a big issue. There's no downsides at all, the devs just suddenly decided to give everyone very strong tools to cover all parts of the game ON TOP of our tower arsenal, some of which is already very overpowered and unbalanced. I will get into the specific use cases of some consumables in a bit, but the point is that no matter what changes you make to the powerups, as long as the way you use them is unchanged, then this is just a buff to our arsenal that was unneeded. matches.title: TDS start guide for noobs

matches.title: TDS Balance is a Mess - An Analysis
matches.snippet: A core part of what separates a good game from a bad one is balance. Unlike graphics or variety, it can be very simple to do, but it can also be very hard at the same time. Whether or not a tower is balanced, often depends on someone uses it. This is extremely true in tower defense simulator, where a tower can be objectively broken, owned by many, yet has no place in the meta, and generally goes unnoted and unused. Tower Defense Simulator, however, is notorious for poor balance. In every version of the game, some towers have been skewed one way or the other. This is in part due to the unique abilities each tower has, and how they interact with each enemy. But that doesn't make balance any less important when every update, a new tower or change smashes the meta into a million bits. Now lets make something clear: some towers being bad isn't going to break the game. What is, however, is when those towers have been part of the meta, or a centerpiece of the game for the longest time. That's what the Overhaul update messed up on: Too many longstanding meta towers being altered. Namely, ranger and cowboy. Not to mention the addition of several new features, and an entire new game mode that was... literally impossible at launch. matches.title: Is fallen the new easy mode?
matches.snippet: Fallen was kicking everyone's ass when it came out last August, including mine which I have old posts about. Since then, a bunch of towers got buffs and changes, 5/6 golden towers, mortar rocketer and pursuit, those 3 have become staples for fallen & strats. The waves got nerfed and a new eco-system was released in March made it so you don't have to be broke anymore. Now we have skill trees which boosts eco into the stratosphere and I can bring Engineer instead of a <=$600 tower, even more DPS! I also recently played a bit with a low level alt account, I can easily win a quad game with the following loadout: Farm DJ Crook Boss Electroshocker & Rocketeer. For most maps, not a single player needs skills or special towers! Easy mode through molten are not much more than quick stepping stones to lvl 30 & fallen, you'll be hard pressed to find anyone there above levels 30-50 & not doing missions. fallen was previously a struggle with public matchmaking and would take 30-35 mins, now I can easily win in <22 mins. It's just as easy as old fallen was this time last year. Power creep is real and I've been wondering a lot of about the long-term direction of TDS, so far it seems like it's been towards buffing both towers and gamemodes. new fallen is still longer and a bit more complex than old fallen, Molten + the 3 special gamemodes got buffed. matches.title: The Worst Tower In TDS
matches.snippet: Now when people think of "The Worst Tower", they usually think Freezer, Archer, Rocketeer, Pyromancer (if you're stupid), and more. But you're wrong, there is one that is extremely lower than the rest, or was at least, that being: Void Miner(VM). Now, due to the void miner being a developer exclusive tower (and handed out to certain people, I can't go in depth on its upgrades, but I will for its purpose {also there's like videos from John Roblox and Wikiacolors on it, so check those for actual info}) The basic premise of the VM is that it mines "corruption", once corruption reaches a certain number, it would activate the now removed Hidden Wave. The tower was created as a way to activate the Hidden Wave without needing to speedrun fallen mode. On paper it sounds good, but when you look into it: oh god it sucks. First off: The VM does nothing other than help activating the wave, it's like farm but doesn't reward you along the way while you invest in it: only to the very end. Now to get the needed corruption value for the Hidden Wave, you need to place and upgrade more VMs, which require cash in game, so not only do you need to focus on beating the game, you also need to put valuable cash in upgrading the VMs, which can make your overall defense weaker or downright lose you the game. Some people read the title and that's what you're here for, so I'll just get all the screenshots then I'll do the nerd talk where I might complain about things. Then I'll go in depth about the challenge and what I think it says about the TDS meta in some ways, real nerd things, if you're just here to see the screenshots I don't mind. Would recommend this challenge though, it's pretty fun This was the first attempt, it was a success, although not a surprise to me personally because I'm using Swarmer. A tower that most people might not think is a top tier, but it's the most cost efficient DPS in the entire game so it made perfect sense. This was just to see how possible moneyless fallen was, and yes that's the term I dubbed for this. I also have Gold Minigunner, so again, really cost efficient DPS just for hiddens. I did another Swarmer run later on, and the Swarmer runs were the only runs where I had enough money by the final wave to afford a Commander micro and Medic micro to place some more Swarmers. Here I just barely failed, the king entered with just around 10k health left. This is possibly the best map I could of chosen for this loadout since the crook minions cover the entire map and have surprisingly good range, the Rangers also cover the entire map, and the Crook boss early game spot and Ranger spot is so close I didn't even need to max the rest of the Commanders to reach all of the towers with the ability. The biggest problem was money, I couldn't max all Rangers until the boss had gotten really far onto the track, and the Toxic gunners, while helpful, were not necessary for other enemies. My mindset behind it was it slows everything down by 25% and I can spam it for lots of DPS, but I had so little money to even upgrade my Rangers that I couldn't do that and it didn't work out. Farm is meta for a reason, but fallen actually proves a very fun challenge for me going moneyless, pretty cool. I learned from my mistakes and decided to use Turret. I chose Turret because it has pretty huge map, having covered majority of the track by time it was maxed and there was a max DJ. I barely won though, fallen king was right in front of the exit with a few thousand health when I sold my Turrets to max the rest of them to make sure he died, then I sloppily placed them as you can see there, I only left one in the original Turret spot next to my early game spot. Not much more to say because I plan to talk about the moneyless challenge itself and what makes it challenging in the summary for nerds. This was my most recent win doing moneyless. I did the exact same thing as my first run except I replaced Gold Minigunner with Gold Crook boss instead to see if maybe I would lose to hidden enemies. It went basically exactly the same as last time, except one shadow boss did leak on wave 37 or 38, so I just placed a maxed Gold Crook boss at the end to kill it then moved it back. It leaked because my towers were stunned, and I only had one Medic that was recharging the ability (I couldn't afford a second one and I didn't have the money to just micro one). I also won with this loadout on my first attempt, so I think Swarmer is by far the best tower for this challenge and I'll talk about that a bit more in the nerd summary. Other attempts without screenshots I easily had more than half of my attempts using this one loadout, all of them having failed, and you might be surprised. Commander, DJ, Accelerator, Gold Scout, Medic; for the life of me, I could not get to wave 30 with this loadout, I also tried the same loadout but I replaced Gold Scout with Militant and I still failed. I was playing somewhat casually, if I'm in the mood I can keep trying this loadout, but I just couldn't do it. Gold Scout dominated early game, not much surprise, probably one of, if not the best early game for moneyless, Accelerator itself was the problem. While Accelerator is no doubt one of the best towers in the game at max level, the levels before it aren't really worth it if you think about it. They aren't awful, they can kill and it gets hidden detection completely free, but a Minigunner, gold variant, or even a Militant can get much better damage worth than an Accelerator from the early levels and are still viable at max. I died on wave 27 two times, one because my Accelerator placement wasn't great since I hoped I could max it to cover a good majority of the track on harbor and the Gold Scouts could carry, that did not work. The other loss, which was much more frustrating, was that I placed Accelerator in the perfect early game position on harbor, and that placement also was my downfall on wave 27 because he ended up targeting the slow boss and the glitches killed me again when that's exactly what I was trying to counter.... rough. Executioner was my early game after tanking first 4 waves, although I'm pretty confident you can place it sooner and be fine in terms of farming for level 4 by wave 13. Why the Executioner is so efficient is because of the new targeting settings, specifically farthest, although last can also work pretty well on long straight paths if you have towers to cover leaked enemies (including hiddens), and even random can work somewhat well. This is the DPS game choice, the backbone of this meta Loadout. Does 2700(450 DPS * 6 Placement limit) DPS in total and that can kill Fallen King in around a minute if you do the math. Although it's Sentries can't deal with hiddens and can't get buffed by DJ and Commander, the gas prices get cheaper and Engineers damage is good enough to kill a shadow boss. It was my idiot ness earlier for saying engineer can't kill a shadow boss. If used properly shadow boss isn't a big deal. Farm. This is the eco choice. Always use farm over cowboy for income generation. I mean yeah Golden Cowboy has shown to make more money than farm, but it depends on the enemies coming. The problem with Commander is Engineer's Sentries, our main DPS, can't be buffed by him. However the gas prices can be cheaper with DJ. Music (Official) Tower Defense Simulator OST - Fallen Boss "oiHSADAsdoisada;lad'111111111111" ―Beginning of Wave 40 (Fallen) Contents [hide] Description Strategy Trivia Version History Description Edit The Fallen King is the final boss in Fallen mode. It moves somewhat slowly (though during Rage Mode, it moves quite fast), but has an outstanding amount of health, has lots of abilities that can stun lots of towers and it can give itself shields, proving to be one of the hardest challenges of the game. It stops to move when performing its Stomp and Block move. The Fallen King appears to be a being of living stone as the boss appears to be entirely made of granite stone. It wears a crown and cape akin to a king's attire, a sword on its right hand radiating purple energy, and a shield on its left hand, all made of stone as well. It is wearing full body armor and appears to be faceless. However, it gains purple eyes and a purple-red aura upon Rage Mode. Unlike its Fallen minions, the Fallen King is immune to being burnt and the Freezer's and Frost Blaster's freeze. In Polluted Wasteland, this does not spawn and is instead replaced by the Nuclear Fallen King. Strategy Edit Using the Electroshocker is the only way to slow down the Fallen King.It can only slow down the Fallen King about 15% for 0.35s per attack.The Fallen King is immune to the Pyromancer's burn and both the Frost Blaster's and Freezer's freeze (even the Ice Age ability for the Freezer).However, the Freezer, Pyromancer and Frost Blaster will continue to attack the Fallen King, and deal damage (not related to their status effect), but the Fallen King will not be slowed down. While the Fallen King blocks he prevents almost all sources of damage. It is immobile while the ability is active, as this is mainly to waste time or waste ability duration.This can be used as a breathing point to manage your troops, but don't use abilities such as the Commander's Call of Arms during this attack.The Fallen King's Block prevents all forms of damage, not including collision damage. Units, like the Military Base Tank, can deal damage to the Fallen King via collision damage. The Fallen King is accompanied by 4 Fallen Guardians. They are always in front of the Fallen King. They should be fought first since they are faster than the Fallen King. Beware of the Fallen King's Stomp attack. This covers an enormous radius around the boss, stunning any ground troops caught in the radius.Cliff troops such as the Outlaw are not affected by this attack.The Medic's ability can cleanse towers, as long as the Medic itself isn't stunned. Outlaws, while immune to the Stomp attack, are not immune to the Spin Slash or Thunderstorm attack. While the Fallen King has a damage shield (during Rage Mode), do not activate John's Gorilla Noises as this is unlikely to increase damage output. Lots of Minigunners, Turrets and Outlaws are recommended against the Fallen King.Make sure to sell any Farms to maximize the number of towers attacking the Fallen King. They don't produce any income anymore, count towards your tower limit, and can be replaced by a more useful towers. It is possible to defeat the Fallen King before he performs his Rage ability, if he is killed quickly enough. This is especially important if you want to activate the Hidden Wave. Trivia Edit The Fallen King has the third highest health pool out of all the zombies in the game, excluding event zombies, with first being the Creator and the second being the Nuclear Fallen King. The Fallen King's sword and shield is very similar to the Epic Golden Sword

verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Hello, this post is about hardcore mode and its problems. Another post complaining about hardcore, crazy, but I've been reflecting a lot and my opinion on hardcore has changed. Flaws with the game in the past and now I think most of what makes hardcore a bad mode in many people's eyes is the difficulty spikes. From an outsider of TDS that might sound stupid: players are complaining about the hard mode being hard, but it's more than that. The enemy types restrict every player to using specific towers to counter the enemy types that appear early on while simultaneously having towers with good damage output for upcoming strong enemies; namely the slow boss, shadow boss, and the three shadow bosses on wave 25. People want hardcore to change itself because of that, and I'll go into flaws with the mode later, but everything I just mentioned isn't a fault with the mode: it's a fault with the game. This goes back to TDS balancing and general, but enemy types weren't well implemented into the game. They added new enemy types, gave some towers the ability to damage these enemies, then expected the players to figure everything out themselves, because it honestly doesn't feel it wasn't play tested in the overhaul update. The developers just didn't give nearly enough towers these detection types, and it almost seems like they didn't have game balancing or game sense in mind at all when assigning what towers can attack them, but more realistic logic instead. The rule they applied to lead was that it can only be damaged by fire, ice, electric, or explosive attacks. In the overhaul update, there was practically no viable tower that could do good damage to leads and enemies in general. The one tower that could was Military base, which was never mentioned that collision damage could damage them. It almost felt unintentional, but whether it was or not doesn't matter because that ended up being the saving grace that made hardcore possible. Then there's flying detection, which I won't go into as much, but you can guess it has the same problem. Only cliff towers could detect flying enemies with Ace pilot and Pursuit as the exceptions. What I'm getting at is the biggest issue is simply the lack of variety; saying a mode is just winnable and that it's fine isn't everything. Having options is important, and let me explain why. Variety is important Let me start with a quick story. So recently I've been testing hardcore, trying to get as far as possible 'stratless'. I used Gold Pyro, farmed, typical hardcore gameplay. I have a low level friend who wants to win hardcore, he sends me the strategy document he has been practicing. I know he still has a lot to learn and I know he probably can't do it 'stratless' (there's a reason I'm typing it like that, I promise) like I'd like to, so I take a read. It's the crown strategy, and it just so happens that what that strategy was doing was nearly identical to what I was doing. What does that mean exactly? Well, I've decided to just learn hardcore more recently and have been looking into it more, and while I didn't have every single thing in the early game exactly the same, I was learning and likely would had come to the same conclusion of how to use the tower optimally in the mode like the document. Well, what does that mean??? It means that hardcore has so little variety, everyone eventually comes to the same conclusion no matter what. There's no such thing as stratless, if you are running hardcore "stratless" as an experienced player, you are running with the tactics you've gained from practicing those strategies you learned and are implementing them. If I'm running fallen, I already know how to deal with the tank, but there I have a variety of towers and loadouts that can help with defeating the tank; some more difficult than others, but nonetheless I know how to optimally farm and when to defend on fallen because of experience, so the term 'stratless' means nothing.Tower defense games are like locks, there are numerous ways to pick that lock with different tools and usages of those tools. Hardcore is like a lock so frustratingly strong, you can only unlock it with the key. Not literally of course, there obviously isn't one single strategy for hardcore, but there are very few because you can only use a few options for hardcore, but these strategies optimize the usage of the towers you do have, so it means with hardcore mode you're always going to learn a strategy. For many like me, using documents isn't fun, but fully being aware that whatever I do to try to learn and progress in hardcore, there is already a group of people that 'unlocked the puzzle' with exactly what I'm trying to do, why would I not resort to that if the goal is just to win? The goal of games is to have fun, but you can't constantly be aware you're trying to have fun to have fun, you're given a destination by the game or yourself and the journey is what is fun. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: So apparently Hardcore got buffed again. And I have a few choice words about the gamemode. You might think I am one of those whiny kids complaining that “I cant get my free wins anymore, waah waaaaah”. Im not. Hardcore is not a free win, and it was not before. And the most recent hardcore buff pushes it into the territory of unintended, unfair, unfun, bullshit. Almost every person i asked, all the videos I watched, all led to the conclusion that hardcore was “too difficult”, “too grindy”, “too long”, and “unfair”. Knowing this, below and the rest of the developer team still decided to release a buff to hardcore. What is the buff, you may ask? The actual placement prices, which used to be bugged, and was normal, has now been fixed to actually be 50% more, like shown. You might think: thats a bug fix, its a good thing. Wrong. Its a bug fix, however, all it did was make a gamemode that was already considered extremely overly difficult to be even more unfun, and difficult. this is a major issue. The 50% upg price increase with 6 farm limit made the gamemode essentially impossible, with only 1 team and a select few with admin commands be able to beat it. In the hardcore update before the most recent one, it was made so that it was returned to its 50% price increase. This was made to increase the difficulty, as some complained that Hardcore was too easy. What was not taken into consideration, however, is that many of the people complaining of the gamemode being too easy, were people using strategies made by others, and often had levels in the late 200s and above. However, the majority of the playerbase does not have this level of skill, and hardcore was simply not easy for us in the slightest. Thus, the price increase returned to 50%, although this time, the gamemode was still possible, due to the farm placement being 8. At this point, hardcore was somewhat rng based, even for very skilled players. No variety in maps played, loadouts used, and whenever you joined a lobby, the majority of players would be looking for players looking for people to join them in their 22nd game of hardcore, as the same player, on the same map, with the same strategy. Hardcore is not fun past your first game. It is the least interesting, most repetitive, and annoying part of the entire game, besides the grind for those 300k coins for golden crate. But thats a separate rant for another day. Now, this version of hardcore that we have now, is even more annoying, difficult, and less diverse than it used to be, if its even possible. Oh another thing that grinds my gears? Abnormals have 6 hp now. If it wasn't bad enough that you have to suffer through an increase in placement price increase, now the zombies are stronger. I am fully aware fallen was in mind with this buff rather than hardcore, but its still a buff to hardcore nonetheless, and a heavy one at that. All of this makes hardcore an unplayable wasteland. And you still have to WIN it 17 times to get a reward that is more than just a skin crate with no influence on actual gameplay. Oh, and one last thing. The defense change is a nice balance, as it makes ranger not the dominant, go to tower to counter defense enemies, without making it a useless tower. However, this heavily hurts hardcore now as well, during the late game, as there is no way to easily counter defense enemies. Right, on to another topic: randoms on hardcore. Hardcore being level 50+, is not okay. You know what I was doing back at level 50 a year ago? Struggling on fallen. Same with these guys. These people, who attempt to get a carry from high level players by joining their lobby and disrupting whatever team is trying to get in a elevator together. This issue only gets worse the higher your level is. level 50s should not be in hardcore. With this new buff to the difficulty of hardcore, this is even more apparent, as suddenly, its becoming close to impossible to get past early game with the essential farming intact, even as a good player. So what do we do about this? Reduce the price increase from 50%, back down to 30%, and increase the starting cash to 800. That would make the early game at least a bit more manageable, and allow us to not have to do a strategy every time. Additionally, buff hardcore rewards too 300 gems. 17 games of hardcore is too much. Another point: bring more maps, preferably slightly easier maps back into rotation. I remember "Robloxia" was pretty good back in beta hardcore testing. Why not bring some of those maps back into rotation again? Definitely more re-playability if there's more maps we can play on, And slap a level 100 limit on playing hardcore, and you're pretty much good to go. It also tanks for the Unknowns, making EVEN MORE STUNS Mega Fast- I mean Mega Slow, Still one of the hardest Hardcore enemies till this day, literally reaches so much further than most of the enemies in Hardcore and serves as an annoying Tank in Wave 23. EXTREMELY Hard Void Reaver, The Final Boss, ofc it's logical to put this boss at the hardest top. Luckily there's only one so Medic shouldn't suffer trying to cleanse all of its stuns. Still gets a lot further than most of the enemies in Hardcore. It's like the Mega Slow of Wave 50, just different, Wait a minute, this is not the hardest enemy in Hardcore?? verified_top_matches.title: Rambling about a tower - the DJ Booth
verified_top_matches.snippet: Sooooo… the DJ Booth. A clear A-Tier tower, powerful but not to the point of being a hard carry. The DJ Booth is useful in essentially every single gamemode and event, save for Rotfield. In Normal, DJ sees the least use, as you generally don’t need expensive towers to beat it easily. In Molten, DJ is always a good option, and is in a very good balance here of ‘great, but not using it doesn’t feel too much like a hindrance’, depending on the strategy you use. In Fallen, DJ shines more than in the prior modes. This time, you’re aiming for more costly towers like the Accelerator if you want to beat Fallen King reliably, and the DJ Booth excels in getting these high DPS towers. The range buff shouldn’t be underestimated either; in fact, it’s extremely strong and may even rival the discount buff. verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Sooooo… the DJ Booth. A clear A-Tier tower, powerful but not to the point of being a hard carry. The DJ Booth is useful in essentially every single gamemode and event, save for Rotfield. In Normal, DJ sees the least use, as you generally don’t need expensive towers to beat it easily. In Molten, DJ is always a good option, and is in a very good balance here of ‘great, but not using it doesn’t feel too much like a hindrance’, depending on the strategy you use. In Fallen, DJ shines more than in the prior modes. This time, you’re aiming for more costly towers like the Accelerator if you want to beat Fallen King reliably, and the DJ Booth excels in getting these high DPS towers. The range buff shouldn’t be underestimated either; in fact, it’s extremely strong and may even rival the discount buff. In Hardcore, it’s almost required to bring along a DJ Booth, though my lack of experience outside of strategies that always use DJ means that I don’t really know how hard DJless Hardcore is. Same goes for Polluted Wasteland and PWII. DJ is essentially the same in all events: extremely beneficial, almost to Hardcore’s extent for some. Nights 1 and 2 are an exception, where you wouldn’t use DJ in the former and commonly only go for Level 3 in the latter. DJ Booth has interesting upgrades. Most increase one or both of his buffs, which is nice. Level 3 is the most popular aside from Level 5, as you get a 10% discount on tower upgrades then, while the other levels only increase range buffs (though once again, they shouldn’t be ignored). I think this is fine, though I would like Level 2 in particular to have a bit more usage. Maybe a 5% discount? It’s extremely small, but could make it worthwhile. I think DJ Booth is fairly decently balanced and needs little to no changes. I’ve talked about skill ceilings back in my Medic ramble, so I’ll do the same here. To be proficient at using the DJ Booth, you need to know: Where to place it What upgrades you should aim for and how to manage your farming around them to your teammates’ requirements And, that’s about it, really. Nothing crazy. One thing I’m guilty of when it comes to other people’s DJs is urging them to get a Level 5 as soon as possible. Granted, it is usually in the mid game, but truth be told, a max DJ isn’t needed if you’re gonna place down just a few towers. A jerk move is to not upgrade anything until the DJ is Level 5 (which I am also guilty of), so don’t do that. The DJ Booth looks really good for what it is. It’s what you’d expect, really. I love the outfit DJ has, along with all the headgear. The audio visualiser is also a sick touch, and it actually displays accurately to the music playing, even if it is custom music. The speakers also go along with the music, another neat detail. DJ Booth, great tower visually. The music that plays is also super catchy. It’s to be expected from Phoqus. We haven’t even started on the skins yet, which are all amazing in their own right. The weakest to most people is Neon Rave, where it is essentially just Default with extra neon. I… like that. I mean, it’s like a direct upgrade to Default. The track that plays, I’m a huge fan of it. I’ll go over Ghost now. It’s the only Ghost skin I like, and by a longshot. The music is an absolute banger, the theme is great and I love the speakers and fire. The one issue I have with it is the lack of an audio visualiser which made Default and Neon Rave so nice. It’s a great skin, though I’m not sure if it’s my favorite out of the three. I will say that this one gets the least hate in general, which I understand, at least compared to this next one… Neko… where do I begin with this one. First off, I won’t hide the fact that I like this skin a lot. It’s a genius theme and a great execution. The music is the only part I don’t like too much, but even then it’s still high quality stuff that I know appeals to many. The main point of interest here is the DJ herself, which, let’s say, sparked a lot of activity within the community when it first came out and when Sledger’s hammer animation was shown off. So much controversy surrounded this skin purely for having a female humanoid, and a ‘furry’ one at that. Some people “””simped”” for her, while others hated her existence. I was really quite neutral, and didn’t care all too much. All I can say for sure is that her presence really showed everyone what the TDS community is made of. Personally, I was just annoyed she didn’t have gigantic speakers like the rest of the skins. People want Classic DJ Booth. I, too, want Classic DJ Booth. Most people who draw Default DJ draw Pre-Overhaul DJ. It makes sense: the design is simple but endearing, and the equipment was pretty unique. Old Neon Rave also gains props for being different from Default at the time and having a huge stage to jam out on. Since I’m an “”””artist””””, I’ll say this much: DJ Booth, all skins, is fucking great to draw. All skins are filled with personality which can be reflected in drawings so wel

Hidden defense: Rangers: never get hidden detection, so they are weak to shadow and hidden bosses. verified_top_matches.title: Is Commander that good?
verified_top_matches.snippet: I said in another post that in my opinion, the Commander was overrated. Many people disagreed with me. But what is the commander all about? The Commander is a tower that buffs firerate and is able to double the amount of DPS at level 3. Does that make it a good tower? It depends on some towers. Towers like minigunner and outlaw? Yes. Starting towers like scout (Non-Golden) and sniper? No. Not at all. However, it still does do something. So I did an experiment. I wanted to beat molten with Starter Towers (Scout (Non-Golden), Sniper, Soldier (Non-Golden), and demoman) with ccommander. It went pretty successful until the mystery boss waves. It was more of a RNG problem, so I tried again. Same results. The Boss 3s- I mean Speedy Bosses went through my defenses. Now I tried it with minigunner, farm, outlaw and military base. I won. (Obivously) I took some damage early-game. It wasn't nothing big. Is commander that good? It depends on the towers you use. But I can definitely say that it helps a lot in hardcore and fallen. It's not needed in modes like molten and normal. Is Commander that good?

They have knowledge about the game, they had experiences, they can actually do stuff like microing Medics or chaining Commander. They are reliable teammates. Just remember to always have an early game tower with you. Things can get arkward when all 4 players are farming and no one is defending early game. The main thing I will be suggesting to balance is to fix the Rate of Fire bug. This is a major bug that has been around in tower defense simulator for at least many months by this point, and it's a major issue. I feel this is also the main reason Ranger is considered one of the best towers in the game. Idk how to fix this, just... do it. I think thats all that needs to be said about this. It's logical, and you know... commando kinda sucks rn. Additionally, add 5 damage to max. I do feel more needs to be done to the commando, but I do not own the tower, so I cannot safely say what exactly needs to be done. Paintballer, Scout, and Sniper needs buffs. Scout and Sniper I feel are just too weak, even for free stuff. increase scout dps to 8 and sniper to 10. Paintballer is... pure garbage. Revert the hidden detection nerf, and buff dps to 15. Medic is probably the worst true "support" tower right now, as it's buffs are negligible. Just make the medic not be able to be stunned. Freezer and Pyromancer used to be great towers, before their respective nerfs. I think the pre-mega freezer was slightly TOO powerful for a 1000 coin tower, but I feel it should do what it did back then, just slightly worse. Pyromancer... Rip. Used to be a great tower in my opinion and I feel was one of the towers that deserved more attention, but there has been a major nerf to it, as well as a terrible rebalance. I think they should just give the pyro it's old ability to slowdown zombies back, up to 25%, as well as it's current defense stripping ability. Additionally, can we please have the old farm's inf placement limit back? Or at least increase it to 10? It's just something I really want, not something thats really unbalanced or something. Shotgunner needs it swat van back. For sure. You already over doubled it shop price, you should probably give it back it's old swat van. It was never overpowered. The fate of rocketeer is sad. In the most recent updates, it was nerfed into the ground. Give us the old rocketeer back, below please. Oh, and do the same with the mortar. With the dj booth, a good idea is to just fix all the bugs surrounding it. With the crook boss, revert the most recent nerf to it. And perhaps make the starting price back down to 600. These changes will make it a great tower again. There must be a buff to the cowboy's damage. Additionally, the amount of cash you gain needs to be slightly increased. It's stupid that you can get like 17 cash or something. Make it a minimum of $20/25. Archer has terrible dps right now. 12 dps at max level is far too low. Maybe it could be fixed by buffing the firerate of the archer to around 1 or so. Additionally, give it more pierce to the archer at lower levels, and increase the lower levels' firerate as well. As for swarmer, ik this is a "tower buffs" suggestion, but can you just slightly lower it's ability's dps. It's a bit op. I don't think a literal spamming abilities on 6.5k cash towers should be able to basically solo the fallen king. verified_top_matches.title: How versatile and useful is Hacker really?
verified_top_matches.snippet: Hacker has 4 different abilities: boosting enemy rewards, cloning, hacking enemies, and slowness but how useful is the tower compared to other towers that could use its slot, like DPS towers? The top and bottom paths costs totals of $96K and $80K respectively. It's been only a day since it came out but so far I don't think its worthwhile in most situations. It's slowness is 15 to 25% which isn't a lot, stunning and freezing towers can do better. It's eco boost definitely doesn't compensate for its very high cost. Unit DPS is inherently low and inconsistent, since it takes a long time for high health enemies has to die first before becoming one with a fraction of its original health. Cloning is imo, the one noteworthy ability, but costs 65% or 90% of the tower cost for the top and bottom paths respectively and can only be used once every 60 secs. So the only tower really worth cloning is Gatling Gun. Thus one really useful for the final waves of the special gamemodes or hardcore. So far I would definitely not recommend bringing it to Fallen and only bring it to special gamemodes or hardcore, to boost much needed single target DPS but only if you or someone else brings Gatling Gun. How versatile and useful is Hacker really?

verified_top_matches.title: TDS for dummies
verified_top_matches.snippet: Go into a match by yourself (important: BY YOURSELF) choose molten mode and spam max level scout until you lose Keep doing that over and over and over until you get minigunner Then do that, but get a minigunner whenever you have saved up enough, get several to level 3. do that over, and over, and over until you get farm. Then spam scout, but place multiple farm at the same time, then spam max mini. Do that over, and over, and over, until you get first the ranger, then the commander By now you should win, just do that over, and over, and over until you hit level 50 and got dj, ace pilot, and military base. By then your towers should be: scout sniper ace pilot military base mini ranger farm commander dj ONLY. your loadout should be the former five. Then switch your loadout to ace and military only, then go into hardcore, place level 3 ace and spam level 2 military base, then spam level 2 ace until you lose. Do that over, and over, and over until you get accelerator. Replace ranger with accel and mini with scout. Win molten over, and over, and over until you get 6 golden skincrates, all towers and all emotes. Then you are ready to play your first multiplayer match. you should only play 4 before returning to solo Hardcore Hidden wave Fallen badlands Frost event Then either keep soloing and/or make new strategy, or quit tds. verified_top_matches.title: (Very Shitty) Tower Idea: Battleship
verified_top_matches.snippet: Now I know I'm piggybacking off of Yeoch's U-Boat Tower Idea but hear me out for a very shitty idea because I'm basically the most brain-dead idiot here. Tower Description: The Battleship is an extremely expensive but extremely powerful tower that can be unlocked for 150,000 coins or 15,000 gems. Players must be level 250 to purchase this tower or 500 to get it for free. In order to balance out its absurd damage, it has an absurd cost to even obtain. However, you cannot bring anything else other than the Farm and must rely on your teammates in order to place down the Battleship. You cannot place it in small waterways nor on land as it is a huge naval vessel. This is an Admin-Only tower as it is far too powerful for public users and will make the game unfairly easy. I will explain what this does to the general gameplay and how it may affect the future of the game if it not heavily changed or removed. I will offer solutions to every issue I point out afterwards, as I do believe this mechanic can add something meaningful to the game, but the devs messed it up in every single manner and it was overall unnecessary, and I believe many other things should of been prioritized over this. How will consumables affect gameplay in matches? Firsly, the fact that these are just a direct upgrade to a player's arsenal is a big issue. There's no downsides at all, the devs just suddenly decided to give everyone very strong tools to cover all parts of the game ON TOP of our tower arsenal, some of which is already very overpowered and unbalanced. I will get into the specific use cases of some consumables in a bit, but the point is that no matter what changes you make to the powerups, as long as the way you use them is unchanged, then this is just a buff to our arsenal that was unneeded. At best, powerups are an optional way to play that gives the player more utilities that are fun and enjoyable, no issue to obtain and use outside of matches, and are completely optional, making it a generally unnecessary mechanic in the first place when a new mode could of been developed instead, but still something to enjoy. At worst, you get everything TDS did, which is the complete opposite of what I just described There is also the possibility that TDS devs will balance gamemodes around the use of these powerups because of power creep, so playing without powerups will not be viable anymore and you will NEED to constantly supply yourself with consumables to win harder modes. The balancing of some consumables with examples On top of being a guaranteed buff to our arsenal, every single consumable is good, and a good amount of them, even low tier ones, make the game extremely easy. It costs the player nothing in a match to do any of the following examples: Farm at wave 0 and spam barricades as your defense. 150 hp barricades are extremely good early defense for free. Spam supply crates early on in the game to get high level Farms or good defense. Works especially well with the tactic above. You can get all level 3 Farms before wave 8 and just instantly get an Accelerator. You don't even need to bring an early game tower anymore. Nobody has to in a quad. For modes with enemies too strong for barricades to handle in the early game, use molotovs and grenades to handle them. Yet another viable early defense completely for free. Use molotovs, grenades, airstrikes, or napalm strikes to do problematic waves for you if you don't want to defend and keep building your eco. i.e wave 20 fallen, wave 7 pw2, etc. Use a nuke on the final wave and kill everything except the boss, with only a few exceptions in some harder modes that are still heavily damaged by the nuke. 50k damage on EACH INDIVIDUAL ENEMY, which can be over a million damage in a single click, for FREE. There is no cost in a match to using a nuke. No insane price barrier to prevent you from spending that money on a Mercenary base micro or something. No downsides at all. "But they just make the game too easy because gamemodes aren't balanced around them. The future gamemodes should be balanced around these powerups and they will be fun and strategic to use." NO. Again, these cost nothing to use in-game, so if anything, a gamemode balanced around the use of overpowered powerups will just lock players out of being able to play without powerups. However, the biggest issue with this argument is that consumables, unlike towers, are a limited resource. You need to buy each individual barricade, supply crate, nuke, and whatever else you use. I will get into the issue of obtainability and supply of consumables. Obtaining consumables and the problem with limited supply As the name implies, these are one-time use items, meaning you need to own multiple and constantly supply yourself with them. A mid grade crate costs 750 coins, which is more than a fallen game triumph, and gives you 6 items. I myself have plenty of coins to spend on these, but a newer player will struggle to get these on top of needing permanent towers to buy. Having a limited resource that you constantly need to supply outside of the actual game to be able to use in-game is a terrible idea, as it is just obnoxious and forces the player to spend more playtime grinding simply to be able to use these powerups for their games. Not to mention that it's luck-based to get the powerups you want like a nuke, so it's not even guaranteed. "But the powerups are not necessary and are just a boost to your game. You do not need to constantly supply them because it's not necessary to win." Then why even implement this mechanic? You can get 40 unbuffed minigunners to get 8 THOUSAND dps, with maxed skill tree that adds up to TEN THOUSAND It is a very simple tower, having only one gimmick being it’s rev up time, this beast of a unit can fully take buffs because rev time doesn’t affect it’s DPS the moment it starts attacking, meaning if you had dj and a commander chain. You get 4 THOUSAND MORE DPS FROM SACRIFING 4 MINIS and this is without max skill tree mind you. This is the de-facto DPS tower in solo and organized duos #2 Strongest division of TDS, The Mercenary Base This tower rewards skill the most out of any other, if you know when, how and where to use it’s units, you get unmatched DPS. A Quick introduction, Rifleman is the standard single Target unit with large range at the cost of being faster and weaker in HP, grenadier is the splash damage unit with weaker single Target and range but with higher health and defense. Riot guard is the frontliner, keeping your stack of riflemen and grenadiers alive by rushing and killing any enemies that gets too close, it is very fast, has melee range and has stalling capabilities, Finally, the Field medic, it’s the back liner of the army, it gives units a shield that breaks upon any impact but tanks the damage of said attack and regens slowly while also giving back hp to damaged units. Now, looking at the 2 DPS units, their DPS numbers are pretty weak, especially for the tower’s price. This is where the base’s best playstyle comes in, stacking. What is stacking? Stacking is when units that stop to attack enemies keep attacking in one common spot, slowly creating this mini army/group of units in one « stack » usually having a few hundred DPS. The rifleman and grenadier push this to the limit. Before getting to the DPS numbers, this tower also has another up side. Detection coverage, unlike many towers, the rifleman has hidden and flying detection starting from level 3, which is a pretty cheap price for effective flying in frost/fallen. Grenadier and riot guard are both and effective anti lead options but grenadier has splash damage while riot guard’s collision can hit hidden enemies. The mercenary base can effectively cover every detection with good DPS numbers too. Finally, its DPS potential, its only small issue is that its DPS has to build up and has to be maintained. But in a good rifleman only stack from one mercenary base, you csn get 1 thousand DPS that destroys any hidden , flying or boss enemy with ease. While the grenadier is weaker in terms of single Target, having 600 DPS, it has a big explosion radius, making it guaranteed to have more than one target in non boss situations at the cost of no common detections except for lead. Finally the riot guard, this shouldnt be your main dps from mercs unless all your stacks died and your other DPS is struggling, she is a saving grace for you and your stack. Having every AirDrop Activated at once can deal 18 thousand damage that ignores defense and damages any non flying enemy in sight. It’s DPS output was so overpowered the devs added Lifetimes to units just to prevent infinite stacking 😭😭😭 A versatile tower usable for any and every situation in the late game that can be placed thrice meaning all of this is tripled. #1 Queen of all trades, The Engineer What tower can cover early-late game DPS, every detection for a cheap price and splash damage? The goat of TDS, Engineer can do all of that and more too! She costs 600 dollars to place down and has pretty decent cost efficiency, making her a viable early game tower in a DPS oriented loadout. She covers the 2 nicher detecions (flying and lead) starting from base level, making her an insane tower for early hc/vc, and 2 cheap upgrades later, you get hidden detection not just on her but her sentries as well for the total cost of 1925. You cover every detection very effectively in the early game for less than 2k She is a pretty expensive tower to max out, costing 52k in total, and she has a placement limit of 6, making her a pretty late game investment , but also your first. She is consistently cost efficient with minor differences in her late levels, meaning you can get 372 dps or 2.2k total DPS for pretty cheap! Her main source of damage in her mid-late levels is her sentries, which are units who can’t get stunned or debuffed, effectively giving her stun and debuff immunity and having pretty decent boss killing capabilities. For events, EVERY boss event has been done solo, including the recent Vortex Dark Castle week, the Haunted Lych week without MK, and the obnoxious Chutes Vortex week. Of all the TD games I have played, only TBz may not be solo friendly as Expert mode on harder maps are probably impossible solo, but its not as solo-unfriendly as TDS, where every single event except TWO, and every special gamemode is unbeatable solo. In TD games, solo-able gamemodes are the norm among the most popular TD games, and gamemodes in TDS are supposed to be exception which are generally frowned upon by the BTD6 community. You should have seen their rage when they discovered that a map on CHIMPS (Muddles and Bloodles in early versions, Ravine in the verison of its release) was not possible solo, and their developers fixed that ASAP. But the TDS community treat solo-impossible gamemodes as the norm now, and they just say "get some friends, its not supposed to be beatable solo" like they ever played a TD game outside of roblox, the true chad TD games. Even among TD games in roblox, TDS is the most solo-unfriendly one ever. In TB events, you CAN win with randoms, they just need to have rail/phaser, golden commando is NEVER needed. In TBz all you need is a little extra firepower and early-game support, you don't need precise and skilful teammates. Compare that to TDS, where you absolutely, need, NEED, NEED friends in real life to beat special gamemodes and events consistently. All of you have to strictly follow a strategy, which is NOT FUN. They either need to be beside you, or on a Discord call. Not only that, you need MULTIPLE friends online at the same time, for FIFTY MINUTES STRAIGHT. As a student, this is especially hard to do since everyone's schedule is different. Either that or you need just ONE friend, but he/she HAS TO HAVE BOTH accelerator and engineer. And very, very little people can be bothered to grind 7,000 gems especially if they don’t have much time. It seems like the only people that can beat these gamemodes in TDS are people without anything outside of gaming and have nothing to do for hours on end, and have one or multiple friends who are the same. And considering most players on roblox are either middle or high school students, the developers reach to their target audience very poorly. Please fix this issue and make all special gamemodes beatable solo. This can really help people who don’t have much time on their hands. Some suggestions I can give: Suggestion 1: More than 5 tower slots. In TDS, there are multiple types of enemies with immunities with many types of towers to counter each type of immunity, which in turn are vulnerable to another type of enemy immunity. This is very similar to BTD6, except that in TDS, all the types of immunity can spawn (leads, flying, hidden) BUT YOU ARE LIMITED TO 5 TOWERS. In BTD6, all immunities can spawn, but you also get all the towers. You will need farm, commander, DJ and medic which already takes up 4 tower slots, leaving only ONE available. It MUST be an early game tower or else you will lose before you even get your ranger down. But then you’re gonna lose in the late game anyway since a tower that’s cheap to place is cheap to upgrade and not enough damage for final boss. So you need to sacrifice one support for an early game option and late game option. That’s still not enough as flying enemies exist. So you must use golden cowboy (again, very difficult to unlock and its RNG based) as economy and use something against flying/leads. verified_top_matches.title: TDS start guide for noobs
verified_top_matches.snippet: This is a pretty easy start guide, and this will lead to your success. this will only really lead you to level 50, so keep that in mind. before you do anything, go into a game, any game. no matter what people say, DO NOT unequip sniper. I'm not saying that sniper is good, I'm saying this for the experience of having sniper and using it to get a feel for the game. play a game, preferably a map that is easy or normal. a gun with the mode on the screen will pop up. chose molten, it will reward you more and is around the same difficulty. play through the game, you must make sure the blue circle around the towers is in range of the path the zombies walk on. the tower with the pistol(called the scout) and the tower with the sniper(the sniper) are the 2 towers you have. the sniper you can only place on certain elevated spaces, and the scout you can place almost anywhere on the ground. try to place towers where the blue circle(which is there range)is on the path the most. get a feel for the game. after losing and realizing how hard the game is, go back to the lobby. when you get back, do not buy a soldier, demoman, paintballer, or freezer. it's usually better to have an empty slot, and in the soldiers case, it's good not to have so you will have more of a success in getting golden towers if you wish to later on. also unequip sniper. it's incredibly trashy and is one of the worst towers

What you want to do is save for the best tower in the game, the farm. either grind a bunch of games until you can hit 2000 gold, or just play with other people. Once you hit that magical 2000, buy the farm. What it does is that it will give you money at the start of each wave, and the higher the upgrade, the more the money. After that, grind, or play with other people until you get ace pilot. it's a good noob tower, and after a recent buff, you might actually help. how the ace pilot works is that it will fly around the edge of its range, shooting zombies below it. play a game by yourself and get a feel for it. by the way, if you ever get any wins, go to the rewards tab, and go and look around the area. you should be able to find a reward for the mode you beat. By the way, if you hit level 30, DO NOT redeem crook boss. Its not a good tower, and it will lessen you chances of getting a good golden tower later on. After that, grind or play with other people until you get 2,500 coins. This is a tower I have been using to grind in molten for a very long time. It’s one of the early game towers, and you should use it in the late game until you start getting better towers like ranger or turret. The loadout you currently have should be scout,farm, ace pilot, and military base. After this, you can probally want to grind untill you get 5000 coins, which is a lot, but it’s worth it. After getting 5000 coins, get the minigunner tower. This is one of the best towers in the game, and as a level 75-80 person, i still prefer to use this tower in fallen rather then accelerator(as long as i'm not in mega servers lol) this is a long range(for a ground tower) and has i high fire rate. Test this tower out. You will be very surprised on what it can do. After this, grind to 3,500 coins to get commander. How this tower works, is that when i gets to level 2, go to its upgrade menu and click that little icon you dont see on other towers. Any tower in its range will get a firerate boost. Now you have a pretty good loadout. You should have minigunner, commander, farm, military base, and scout. You get rid of scout if you want to lol. If you want something else to replace scout, i recommend shotgunner or ace pilot. After that, grind to 8,500 coins, which is A LOT of coins, so it might take a few hours for 2 days. Then you should get the ranger tower, which is the sniper tower, but very good. It does not have hidden detection, so be careful. After buying that, start grinding to level 50, and you should be able to redeem turret, and boom, now your level 50 and you can either grind hardcore or use robux to get accelerator. This tower is great for molten, Badlands, or hardcore mode alongside ace pilot, but it’s still better to skip this tower and head for ace pilot/farm first. This tower can be used in strats, but only if they are for beginners or needed for early defense. Soldier is an amazing/good for people new to the game as it is really cheap to buy and due to the upgrades being so cheap youd pretty much get hidden detection in the first five waves. Hunter: This tower is even worse than sniper despite costing coins in the shop. This tower is slow, weak, and you just should not buy it until you have everything else in the game. It does have flying detection, however ace pilot is much better at dealing with flying enemies. INTERMEDIATE: Militant: Militant is a very decent tower It has decent dps, cheap hidden detection, and is a solid tower for early game, as well as transitioning into a decent sub-dps in the late game. Medic: This tower has the unique and valuable ability to unstun towers at level 5 In addition bout the ability to unstun, it has the ability to heal base health over time. It’s difficult to fit medic into a loadout in solo, cause DJ and commander are more essential. Its cost efficiency is very bad, meaning this tower shouldn’t be used until stunning enemies come. However in duos, trios, and quads, it is an invaluable tower to have unless its fallen mode. Freezer: Freezer is a decent tower for ONLY stalling. It’s good at stalling enemies, however it’s bad damage means it must be with another dps or stalling tower. DPS towers already deal enough damage to comfortably kill enemies without relying on freezer unless your JustHarrison and want to do the VS. Series. The Freezer is especially useful when paired with towers that have long charge-up times or a high firerate. Farm: Farm is MUST GET TOWER when starting to play tds and farm is probably the most essential tower in the game This tower should be a part of every match you play. Soloing some game modes does give enough money that it isn’t needed, however farm itself gives you enough money for anything necessary to beating a gamemode. Shotgunner: Shotgunner is a good tower However, it’s great for speedruns, as it’s high damage output in a quick amount of time means it can kill early game zombies quite fast It’s outclassed by gladiator and gold scout, however the difficulty to obtain them means there’s no point in using them in strats unless it’s a wr speedrun. Shotgunner excels in molten mode, where if used correctly does NOT leak and is also used in the NST molten speedrun world record. Military Base: This tower semi-decent It does deal half-decent damage, but it’s so slow and boring that you’ll probably fall asleep before the game ends. The units deal decent DPS, but they will take a lot of damage from the boss’s attacks, reducing their damage by a lot. The only upside is that this tower’s units are unstunnable. Rocketeer: Rocketeer sucks Its performance at earlier levels is bad, due to its slow firerate. It has a massive deadzone, meaning it must be placed far from the path and is only utilized well in certain maps like four seasons. Its small splash radius means only one or two enemies will be hit for full damage, meaning it has to be used against clumped up hordes to be utilized fully. It does have an extremely high range for a ground tower, covering a lot of the map. Ace Pliot: This tower is very versatile, being a great early defense for every gamemode It’s flying detection allows it to serve as a great counter to early-game balloons in hardcore mode Its DPS at level 5 allows it to be a good counter to souls as well as a secondary late-game option. verified_top_matches.snippet: Hello. I've been thinking about talking about the new recent balancing changes for awhile, though I've procrastinated and they've just kept happening. I will talk about the tower rebalances, what I think of them, and giving some suggestions for improvements. Just in case anyone really thought to themselves "I want to hear that guy's opinion on x" then here it is. Very long as usual. Tower rebalances I'll go over what I think about the rebalanced towers, starting with: GOLD COWBOY A highly deserved nerf for a long time coming, I think this was a very positive change. The only negative I could see to this change among other tower changes was the intention behind it, mainly wondering if it's because the devs don't want solo hardcore to be possible. That aside though, this was a very good change since this was by far the best gold skin and easily one of the best towers in the game; an easy high S tier tower. I've seen my favorite TDSman WikiaColors argue that the Gold Cowboy had the "niche" of being able to solo fallen and hardcore. My argument against this is that it wasn't a niche at all, it was an extremely versatile tower and that's why it was so good at those two things. That aside though, this was a very good change since this was by far the best gold skin and easily one of the best towers in the game; an easy high S tier tower. I've seen my favorite TDSman WikiaColors argue that the Gold Cowboy had the "niche" of being able to solo fallen and hardcore. My argument against this is that it wasn't a niche at all, it was an extremely versatile tower and that's why it was so good at those two things. It's not just that though, as I can say that you could easily use pre-nerf Gold Cowboy in nearly any mode and it would do incredibly well as a Farm replacement, even in quads, as long as there aren't more than two people using it. Early game for pw2 (up to wave 16 is what I've seen for using only Gold Cowboys)? Check. Early-mid game for pizza party? Check. Early game for badlands? Check. All you had to do for any of these modes was have someone do early a bit with anything half decent, like Ace pilot on pw2, then have the Gold Cowboy player just start spamming level two. Either that, or you can leak the very first wave(s) and just have two Gold Cowboy players both spamming level two. They get them to level three for the hiddens, and everything was covered. The only situations I can name where this tower isn't good is lost souls and quickdraw, and that is due to having four wasted slots on lost souls, so every player's fifth slot needs to be essential to the game, mostly late game and hoards, as the lost souls loadout covers early game. The other is quickdraw since you just need to speedrun, and Gold Cowboy doesn't do things quickly. Gold Cowboy's uses are not niches, the things Gold Cowboy wasn't good for were the niches. I still believe that Gold Cowboy is the best gold skin even after the nerf, though it's a lot more debatable now. ENGINEER Also a highly deserved nerf and one I'm very happy about. Early game on this tower got nerfed pretty hard and that was my biggest gripe with this tower. People would argue in favor of the tower saying that its intended purpose was to be an all-rounder. I say this then: Have you thought that the towers intended purpose is just silly? Are you telling me that the TDS devs and balancers always have the best judgement, and so their intent is what it should be? No shame to them, as I think they've done an incredible job with the game recently, but I am saying that people make mistakes and it has happened many times with this game. The way I would want this tower to be is if it were subpar for the entirety of the game, where it can be used for any portion of the game, but just not very good at it, as there are clearly better options in every case. For the most part, this nerf has done that, as the early game and even mid game has been killed on this tower, but it still does decent damage, just can't do things alone. I think the final level is still too good for what you're paying, as it is still very cost effective, especially since this tower isn't punished for stuns nearly as much as others. I would nerf this by nerfing the max dps a bit further or changing how the sentry works, making it so if the Engineer is stunned, then it doesn't fire. I think that second solution is pretty lame though, as I do enjoy the mechanic of using units for dps, so I'd say nerf the war machine sentries a bit so it has around 250~ dps. Keep in mind that the sentries have 22 range and, most importantly, are partially stun immune. They are pretty much invincible with Medic, so I think it's fair to do this. It will still be more cost effective than the other late game towers without supports, but with supports it will be outclassed. RANGER I know this one was awhile ago, but I never talked about it and it will be quick. I think this tower is beautifully balanced, and generally every upgrade feels worthwhile yet not overpowered. The exceptions to this are levels three and five. Even before Ranger's buff, in the midst of Accelerator winning the old time Accelerator vs. Ranger, level three has always been a really good level. And now it's even better; an extremely spammable level. High range, good dps, stun immune, very cost effective level. Max level is also pretty cheap for how much you're getting. 128 dps monster with stun immunit

Tower Defense Simulator, however, is notorious for poor balance. In every version of the game, some towers have been skewed one way or the other. This is in part due to the unique abilities each tower has, and how they interact with each enemy. verified_top_matches.title: Is fallen the new easy mode?
verified_top_matches.snippet: Fallen was kicking everyone's ass when it came out last August, including mine which I have old posts about. Since then, a bunch of towers got buffs and changes, 5/6 golden towers, mortar rocketer and pursuit, those 3 have become staples for fallen & strats. The waves got nerfed and a new eco-system was released in March made it so you don't have to be broke anymore. Now we have skill trees which boosts eco into the stratosphere and I can bring Engineer instead of a <=$600 tower, even more DPS! I also recently played a bit with a low level alt account, I can easily win a quad game with the following loadout: Farm DJ Crook Boss Electroshocker & Rocketeer. For most maps, not a single player needs skills or special towers! Easy mode through molten are not much more than quick stepping stones to lvl 30 & fallen, you'll be hard pressed to find anyone there above levels 30-50 & not doing missions. fallen was previously a struggle with public matchmaking and would take 30-35 mins, now I can easily win in <22 mins. It's just as easy as old fallen was this time last year. verified_top_matches.snippet: Scout: Very bad unless if you have the golden skin for it. Sniper: This was quite decent Pre-Hardcore, now it's just only for VERY, VERY early waves. Paintballer: Trash. Militant: (I don't have any opinion on this tower) Farm: Very good if you have something like the minigunner. Pyromancer: The only Golden skin that doesn't even do anything good. Even though you could still solo it back in 2021, there was still actual difficulty and challenge to it, even I couldn't do it back then. But now that its been 5 years since then, there's no strategy needed for fallen mode, you can just place towers anywhere and win as long as you have like 1-2 towers with flying detection. Frost: Why? Why bring this back? For what reason? You brought back Frost Invasion for 2025 (Although under a different name)? That's fine, we've had Ducky D00M return at that point, but make Frost Invasion into a MAIN GAMEMODE??? FOR WHAT??? You're defiling the grave of a 5 year old event, let Frost Invasion rest at this point. There's no point in even trying to solo grind it either for coins/exp/gems (you get gems from this mode). But even with the gem reward, there's STILL no point in grinding this mode as you can solo hardcore and get more gems for doing so (even if you DON'T kill Void Reaver, you still get more gems than ONE Frost Mode win.) There is no point in this gamemode, let frost invasion die and stop trying to nostalgia-bait the people who played the 2021 Frost Invasion Hardcore: I know it's getting a rework in a month so this is gonna be outdated real fast, but I should still say this now. HARDCORE SHOULD NOT BE POSSIBLE SOLO. I remember having to use google docs with guides in them showing you where to place every tower, because it was that hard. Now you can solo it and make it to wave 50 without any effort, hell, I did that on my first try returning to this game. I just pray they make Hardcore actually hard again with the rework. So that is my opinion on the main 6 gamemodes, alongside Hardcore. Do you agree with this, why or why not? Also, I will make a part 2 to this where i cover the special gamemodes (Badlands, Polluted Wastelands II, Pizza Party). Thank you for reading.
